gbm_population_evidence.quote: Participants must have newly diagnosed histologically confirmed primary glioblastoma or gliosarcoma

candidate_evidence.quote: [EXPERIMENTAL] Arm 1: Nivolumab + Ipilimumab 1mg/kg + TMZ (interventions: Drug: TMZ; Drug: Nivolumab; Drug: ipilimumab 1mg/kg)
To study people with newly diagnosed GBM or gliosarcoma to look at the changes in immune cells in the blood of those who take ipilimumab and nivolumab, along with temozolomide.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Participant must have completed chemoradiation (external beam radiation with concurrent temozolomide) a maximum of 5 weeks prior to initiation of study therapy.

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: ELISPOT functional analysis of CD4+/8+ response to common recall antigens will be used to determine systemic response to ICI treatment.
Determine if T cell response to immune checkpoint inhibitors measuring the change in the pre-treatment and post-treatment blood correlates with progression-free survival

role_evidence.quote: [EXPERIMENTAL] Arm 2: Nivolumab + Ipilimumab 3mg/kg + TMZ (interventions: Drug: TMZ; Drug: ipilimumab 3mg/kg; Drug: Nivolumab)

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: The immunosuppressive nature of GBM may be reversible with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) treatment

coder_notes: Ipilimumab is registered as two interventions (1 mg/kg and 3 mg/kg) that differ only in dose between the two experimental arms; coded as one agent row. Adjuvant TMZ is identical in both arms (soc_backbone). Target engagement coded yes on the basis of planned peripheral-blood T-cell/immune pharmacodynamic measures of ICI response; no tumour molecular biomarkers are registered. Condition list also includes 'Malignant Glioma' but inclusion criteria restrict to glioblastoma or gliosarcoma.
